title: Our claim: Scripture proves Christian doctrine distinctly, not only in seed
source_text: XII. In hac autem disputatione sententia nostra non est omnia religionis Christianae instituta, & fidei dogmata confuse solum atque generatim ex Scriptura probari posse sed distincte & sigillatim, adeoque, hoc quidem sensu, dici posse in Scriptura expresse contineri non virtute tantum, atque in semine.
pass_a_gloss: But in this dispute our opinion is not that all institutions of the Christian religion, and dogmas of faith, can be proved from Scripture only confusedly and generally, but distinctly and sigillatim, and therefore, in this sense indeed, can be said to be contained expressly in Scripture not by virtue only, and in seed.
pass_b_english: In this dispute we do not say Christian ordinances and dogmas of faith can be proved from Scripture only in a general, mixed way.
We say they can be proved distinctly, item by item — and in that sense can be said to stand expressly in Scripture, not merely by force and in seed.

lemmas.latin: non virtute tantum, atque in semine
lemmas.gloss: not by virtue only, and in seed

choices.why: Here the looser sense from XI, against seed-only.
